content.text: {"relation":"DIVERGENT","consensus_summary":"All three blind responses identify lamp oil primarily as the Holy Spirit — His indwelling presence, grace, empowerment, and anointing — grounded chiefly in Matthew 25:1-13, Zechariah 4, and the anointing motif (1 Sam 16:13; Acts 10:38). Recognized alternatives include readiness with no allegorical referent, good works/charity (patristic), genuine saving faith, and grace; the responses agree the Spirit reading is dominant popularly though not academically settled.","book_summary":"The book defines lamp oil as the pressed, tested fruit and evidence of the Spirit's work — proven obedience made manifest, stored up and burned to give light — and explicitly denies that the oil is the Spirit Himself, expressly flagging the 'Holy Spirit' identification as the common view it departs from.","rationale":"The book's entry directly negates the consensus core ('not the Spirit Himself'), displacing the dominant identification rather than sharpening it. While its reading has family resemblance to the 'good works/charity' and 'genuine inward life' alternatives listed by the blind responses, the book's specific formulation — Spirit-produced, proven obedience as the fruit that fuels light, distinguished from both the Spirit and mere works — is framed as a correction of the recognizable common interpretation. An explicit contradiction of the majority meaning, with the book itself noting the common view it rejects, fits DIVERGENT rather than REFINED (which requires compatibility) or NOVEL (since the good-works/evidence family is represented in the consensus alternatives).","citation_support":"PARTIAL","strongest_objection":"Zechariah 4:6 — printed with the entry itself — is the passage where the oil-fed lampstand is interpreted as 'by my spirit,' which most naturally identifies the oil with the Spirit rather than with its fruit; none of the cited texts explicitly equates oil with obedience or the Spirit's produced fruit, so the book's central claim rests on an inferential chain (beaten olive + Ezek 36:27 + Matt 5:16) rather than a direct textual identification.","confidence":"high"}
